mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% over a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, increasing recession risk and prompting equity investors to demand higher risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, or the average forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals weakening aggregate demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and triggering a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in joint regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 94.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real economic output, increasing the likelihood of earnings revisions downward and triggering negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 94.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the year-over-year growth of real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 3.0% signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate sales visibility and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances when RSAFS yoy growth exceeds 3.0%, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and persistently low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) indicates a policy dilemma where inflation is accelerating but monetary tightening is delayed, increasing real rate uncertainty and leading to negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of instances when both CPIAUCSL > 220.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 9.0% signals a labor market collapse, increasing recession fears and triggering a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 130500 and UNRATE > 9.0%, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months, combined with weak residential construction (HOUST < 560), indicates a deepening demand contraction, reducing corporate investment and consumption expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 < 13270 and HOUST < 560, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).
